note: Machine-readable lever dictionary for the tuning mode. Measured values are the reference host (2x RTX PRO 6000, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash); calibration values, never universal claims. generator_map names the placement_calc.py CLI flag or JSON plan field the lever feeds.

levers.what_it_moves: share of routed-expert traffic resident in VRAM vs streamed from DRAM on the CPU tier
levers.direction: more GPU experts -> higher C1/C4, less VRAM for KV/chunk
levers.when_it_helps: always, on a CPU-hybrid MoE; it is the biggest decode lever

measured.result: C1 +6.3% wall, C4 +9.2%; 779 MiB free worst case
+2.5% C1 wall for -40% prefill; NLL +0.0088 fails the gate
prefill +38/+47%; C1 wall -1.9%; NLL in band

levers.what_it_moves: which CPU-resident experts the router actually hits (CPU route share)
levers.direction: checkpoint order = random split; fitted static map = ~15%; runtime = 1-3%
levers.cost: zero VRAM; a permutation is routing-exact, not bit-exact
levers.when_it_helps: whenever experts must live on the CPU tier
levers.reopen: runtime placement: copy_experts_weights_mxfp4 + vendor ktransformers PR #2093; watch SGLang Paged Experts (PR #42557) and llama.cpp --moe-expert-cache (PR #27861, LRU beats static hot lists)

levers.what_it_moves: how many tokens the CPU expert pass may lag the GPU pass
levers.direction: higher D hides the CPU tier; quality breaks at the edge
levers.cost: no memory; D=5 fails NLL (+0.00287) and greedy diverges at 9-39 chars; D=6 loses 0.23 nats
levers.when_it_helps: always on a CPU-hybrid MoE; +22% C1 at D=4

levers.what_it_moves: CPU-tier GEMV throughput on a bandwidth-bound tier
levers.direction: 16 is the plateau; above physical cores it collapses
levers.generator_map: not modeled; fixed 16 on the reference host

levers.what_it_moves: whether scheduler/tokenizer threads float onto CPU-tier worker cores
levers.direction: auto pins to SMT siblings of workers

measured.result: C4 106 or 123 on the same serve (bimodal)

levers.what_it_moves: VRAM share of KV and the served concurrency shape
levers.direction: bigger context/slots -> more KV VRAM, more concurrency
levers.cost: kv_bytes_per_token x context x slots; ladder 512K/1M needs fraction 0.962

levers.what_it_moves: TTFT vs decode rate vs expert capacity (fused-MoE workspace scales with chunk)
levers.direction: bigger chunk -> faster prefill, fewer experts, slightly slower decode
levers.cost: workspace VRAM (7 experts per 4096->8192 step on the reference host)
levers.when_it_helps: coding-agent (first-turn TTFT); hurts multi-user decode slightly

levers.what_it_moves: whether decode batches run captured vs eager
where lookup tables live and how rows are fetched
levers.direction: ahead/chunk-ahead prefetch overlaps Engram I/O with compute
levers.cost: host DRAM or NVMe I/O budget

measured.result: does not fit this host (-78 GiB)
cannot shrink page-cache footprint (~190 KiB/first-touched token)
-0.2..-0.4 s per cold TTFT; default off

levers.reopen: row cache (T3.48) pairs with admission prefetch for C4-heavy admission

levers.what_it_moves: draft-token multiplication of the CPU-expert traffic
levers.direction: more drafts -> more verify traffic on a bandwidth-bound tier
levers.cost: decode quality risk (rejected-draft state corruption measured)
levers.when_it_helps: copy-heavy single-user only, and only after a CPU-tier change

measured.result: +60/+76% C1 copy prompts, -26% review, -63% C4, decode-state defect (-20.5 nats token)

levers.generator_map: not modeled; default off; must pass spec-consistency.py to reopen

levers.direction: lower bpw -> smaller, usually slower/riskier kernels
levers.cost: quality gate re-run for any format change that alters the math
levers.when_it_helps: when the checkpoint as shipped does not fit
levers.reopen: sub-4-bit: a published SM120 EXL3 MoE kernel with a KL number
